# Google Sheets MCP connector

Let your AI work with Google Sheets: read any range or several at once, see a spreadsheet's tabs and sizes, append rows to a table, write and update cells and formulas, create spreadsheets and add or rename tabs. The AnythingMCP connector gives Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Cursor and Gemini 11 MCP tools for Google Sheets: 3 read and 8 can change data.

[![Open Google Sheets in AnythingMCP Cloud](https://img.shields.io/badge/Open%20in-AnythingMCP%20Cloud-1f6feb?style=for-the-badge)](https://cloud.anythingmcp.com/login?mode=register&redirect=%2Fconnectors%2Fstore%3Finstall%3Dgoogle-sheets&utm_source=github&utm_medium=catalog&utm_campaign=google-sheets)

## Start without code

No installation and no terminal: AnythingMCP Cloud runs the Google Sheets connector for you, operated by helpcode.ai in Frankfurt, Germany.

1. **Click the button above** and create an account or sign in. The Google Sheets connector opens, ready to install.
2. **Sign in with your Google Sheets account** when AnythingMCP asks. The first time, an admin creates a small app in the Google Cloud console. Every click is in the [step-by-step guide](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/google-sheets-to-mcp).
3. **Click Install.** AnythingMCP shows the address of your MCP server.
4. **Add that address to your assistant:** [Claude](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-google-sheets-to-claude) · [ChatGPT](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-google-sheets-to-chatgpt) · [Microsoft Copilot](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-google-sheets-to-copilot) · [Cursor](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-google-sheets-to-cursor) · [Gemini CLI](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-google-sheets-to-gemini) · [Meta Muse](https://anythingmcp.com/guides/connect-google-sheets-to-muse).
5. **Ask your first question**, for example: *Open the AccountsReceivable 2026 spreadsheet and show the row for invoice INV-2026-117 from customer Montblanc Solar GmbH*

Prefer help with the setup? [Talk to us](https://anythingmcp.com/contact).

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  client["Claude · ChatGPT · Copilot · Cursor"]
  amcp["AnythingMCP<br/>roles · audit log · encrypted credentials"]
  api["Google Sheets API<br/>sheets.googleapis.com"]
  client -- "MCP, OAuth or API key" --> amcp
  amcp -- "HTTPS, an OAuth 2.0 access token, refreshed automatically" --> api
```

- **The AI client** speaks MCP (Streamable HTTP) to AnythingMCP and only sees tool names, descriptions and results. It never gets the Google Sheets credentials.
- **AnythingMCP** checks the client's role, builds the call from the tool definition, adds the credentials (an OAuth 2.0 access token, refreshed automatically), calls Google Sheets, logs the call and returns the result.
- **Google Sheets** sees an ordinary API client with the rights of the account the credentials belong to.

|---|---|---|

| [`gsheets_append_rows`](#gsheets_append_rows) | Append rows after the last row of the table found in range (e.g. "Sheet1!A:E" or just "Sheet1"), inserting new rows so nothing is overwritten. | write |
| [`gsheets_update_range`](#gsheets_update_range) | Write values into a range, overwriting what is there (e.g. range "Sheet1!B2:C3" with [[1, 2], [3, 4]]). | write |

| [`gsheets_clear_range`](#gsheets_clear_range) | Empty all values in a range (formatting and validation stay), e.g. "Sheet1!A2:Z" to keep the header row. | write |
| [`gsheets_create_spreadsheet`](#gsheets_create_spreadsheet) | Create a new, empty spreadsheet in the root of the user's My Drive, with one sheet named "Sheet1" (or the locale's equivalent). | write |

| [`gsheets_rename_sheet`](#gsheets_rename_sheet) | Rename a sheet (tab). | write |
| [`gsheets_batch_update`](#gsheets_batch_update) | Run Sheets API batchUpdate requests for anything the other tools do not cover: formatting (repeatCell), sorting (sortRange), inserting or deleting rows and… | write |

## Tool reference

Every parameter as the AI client sees it in `tools/list`. Source: [`packages/backend/src/adapters/intl/google-sheets.json`](../../../packages/backend/src/adapters/intl/google-sheets.json).

### `gsheets_get_spreadsheet`

Get a spreadsheet's structure without cell data: title, locale, time zone, URL, and every sheet (tab) with its sheetId, title, position, hidden flag and size (rows, columns, frozen rows), plus named ranges. Call it first to learn the sheet names for ranges.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /spreadsheets/{spreadsheet_id}`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spreadsheet_id` | string | yes | Spreadsheet id, the long string in its link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit. |

### `gsheets_read_range`

Read the cell values of one range in A1 notation (e.g. "Sheet1!A1:D50"). Returns range, majorDimension and values as a list of rows; trailing empty rows and cells are left out. Read large sheets in blocks of rows.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /spreadsheets/{spreadsheet_id}/values/{range}`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spreadsheet_id` | string | yes | Spreadsheet id, the long string in its link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit. |
| `range` | string | yes | Range in A1 notation, e.g. "Sheet1!A1:D20", "'Sales 2026'!A:C" (quote sheet names with spaces), "Sheet1" (the whole sheet), "A2:E" (first sheet) or a named range. |
| `major_dimension` | `ROWS` \| `COLUMNS` | no | "ROWS" (default) returns a list of rows, "COLUMNS" a list of columns. |
| `value_render_option` | `FORMATTED_VALUE` \| `UNFORMATTED_VALUE` \| `FORMULA` | no | "FORMATTED_VALUE" (default, as shown in the UI), "UNFORMATTED_VALUE" (raw numbers; dates as serial numbers) or "FORMULA" (formulas instead of results). |
| `date_time_render_option` | `SERIAL_NUMBER` \| `FORMATTED_STRING` | no | With UNFORMATTED_VALUE or FORMULA: "SERIAL_NUMBER" (default) or "FORMATTED_STRING" for dates and times. |

### `gsheets_batch_read`

Read several ranges of one spreadsheet in a single call, e.g. ["Summary!A1:B10", "Data!A1:F100"]. Returns valueRanges, one entry per range in the same order, each with range and values.

**Access:** read · **Call:** `GET /spreadsheets/{spreadsheet_id}/values:batchGet`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spreadsheet_id` | string | yes | Spreadsheet id, the long string in its link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit. |
| `ranges` | string[] | yes | Ranges in A1 notation, e.g. ["Sheet1!A1:C10", "'Q3 data'!A:A"]. |
| `major_dimension` | `ROWS` \| `COLUMNS` | no | "ROWS" (default) returns a list of rows, "COLUMNS" a list of columns. |
| `value_render_option` | `FORMATTED_VALUE` \| `UNFORMATTED_VALUE` \| `FORMULA` | no | "FORMATTED_VALUE" (default, as shown in the UI), "UNFORMATTED_VALUE" (raw numbers; dates as serial numbers) or "FORMULA" (formulas instead of results). |
| `date_time_render_option` | `SERIAL_NUMBER` \| `FORMATTED_STRING` | no | With UNFORMATTED_VALUE or FORMULA: "SERIAL_NUMBER" (default) or "FORMATTED_STRING" for dates and times. |

### `gsheets_append_rows`

Append rows after the last row of the table found in range (e.g. "Sheet1!A:E" or just "Sheet1"), inserting new rows so nothing is overwritten. Values are parsed like typed input by default. Returns updates with updatedRange and updatedRows.

**Access:** write · **Call:** `POST /spreadsheets/{spreadsheet_id}/values/{range}:append`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spreadsheet_id` | string | yes | Spreadsheet id, the long string in its link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit. |
| `range` | string | yes | The table to append to, e.g. "Sheet1!A:E" or "Sheet1". New rows go after its last non-empty row, starting in its first column. |
| `values` | any[][] | yes | Rows of cell values, e.g. [["Date", "Amount"], ["2026-10-09", 120.5]]. Each inner list is one row; use null to leave a cell unchanged and "" to empty it. |
| `value_input_option` | `USER_ENTERED` \| `RAW` | no | "USER_ENTERED" (default) parses values as if typed in the UI: numbers, dates, percentages and formulas starting with =. "RAW" stores them as plain text exactly as given. |

### `gsheets_update_range`

Write values into a range, overwriting what is there (e.g. range "Sheet1!B2:C3" with [[1, 2], [3, 4]]). Values are parsed like typed input by default, so "=SUM(A1:A9)" becomes a formula. Returns updatedRange, updatedRows and updatedCells.

**Access:** write · **Call:** `PUT /spreadsheets/{spreadsheet_id}/values/{range}`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spreadsheet_id` | string | yes | Spreadsheet id, the long string in its link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit. |
| `range` | string | yes | Range in A1 notation, e.g. "Sheet1!A1:D20", "'Sales 2026'!A:C" (quote sheet names with spaces), "Sheet1" (the whole sheet), "A2:E" (first sheet) or a named range. |
| `values` | any[][] | yes | Rows of cell values, e.g. [["Date", "Amount"], ["2026-10-09", 120.5]]. Each inner list is one row; use null to leave a cell unchanged and "" to empty it. |
| `value_input_option` | `USER_ENTERED` \| `RAW` | no | "USER_ENTERED" (default) parses values as if typed in the UI: numbers, dates, percentages and formulas starting with =. "RAW" stores them as plain text exactly as given. |

### `gsheets_batch_update_values`

Write several ranges of one spreadsheet in a single call, overwriting them: data is a list of {"range": "Sheet1!A1:B2", "values": [[...], [...]]}. Returns totalUpdatedCells and one response per range.

**Access:** write · **Call:** `POST /spreadsheets/{spreadsheet_id}/values:batchUpdate`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spreadsheet_id` | string | yes | Spreadsheet id, the long string in its link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit. |
| `data` | object[] | yes | Ranges and their values, e.g. [{"range": "Sheet1!A1", "values": [["Total"]]}, {"range": "Sheet1!B1", "values": [["=SUM(B2:B99)"]]}]. |
| `value_input_option` | `USER_ENTERED` \| `RAW` | no | "USER_ENTERED" (default) parses values as if typed in the UI: numbers, dates, percentages and formulas starting with =. "RAW" stores them as plain text exactly as given. |

### `gsheets_clear_range`

Empty all values in a range (formatting and validation stay), e.g. "Sheet1!A2:Z" to keep the header row. Cannot be undone through the API, only from the spreadsheet's version history. Installed switched off.

**Access:** write · **Call:** `POST /spreadsheets/{spreadsheet_id}/values/{range}:clear`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spreadsheet_id` | string | yes | Spreadsheet id, the long string in its link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit. |
| `range` | string | yes | Range in A1 notation, e.g. "Sheet1!A1:D20", "'Sales 2026'!A:C" (quote sheet names with spaces), "Sheet1" (the whole sheet), "A2:E" (first sheet) or a named range. |

### `gsheets_create_spreadsheet`

Create a new, empty spreadsheet in the root of the user's My Drive, with one sheet named "Sheet1" (or the locale's equivalent). Returns spreadsheetId, spreadsheetUrl and the sheets; then write with gsheets_update_range and add tabs with gsheets_add_sheet.

**Access:** write · **Call:** `POST /spreadsheets`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | yes | Title of the spreadsheet. |
| `locale` | string | no | Locale for formats and functions, e.g. en_US, de_DE, it_IT (default: the user's). |
| `time_zone` | string | no | IANA time zone for date functions, e.g. Europe/Berlin. |

### `gsheets_add_sheet`

Add a sheet (tab) to a spreadsheet, optionally at a position. Returns replies[0].addSheet.properties with the new sheetId and title.

**Access:** write · **Call:** `POST /spreadsheets/{spreadsheet_id}:batchUpdate`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spreadsheet_id` | string | yes | Spreadsheet id, the long string in its link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit. |
| `title` | string | yes | Name of the new sheet; must be unique in the spreadsheet. |
| `index` | integer | no | Position, 0 = first tab (default: last). |

### `gsheets_rename_sheet`

Rename a sheet (tab). sheet_id is the numeric sheetId from gsheets_get_spreadsheet (0 for the first sheet of a new spreadsheet), not the title. Formulas that refer to the sheet are updated by Google.

**Access:** write · **Call:** `POST /spreadsheets/{spreadsheet_id}:batchUpdate`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spreadsheet_id` | string | yes | Spreadsheet id, the long string in its link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit. |
| `sheet_id` | integer | yes | Numeric sheetId from gsheets_get_spreadsheet. |
| `title` | string | yes | New name; must be unique in the spreadsheet. |

### `gsheets_batch_update`

Run Sheets API batchUpdate requests for anything the other tools do not cover: formatting (repeatCell), sorting (sortRange), inserting or deleting rows and columns (insertDimension, deleteDimension), deleting sheets (deleteSheet), freezing rows, filters, charts. Requests run in order, atomically. Installed switched off.

**Access:** write · **Call:** `POST /spreadsheets/{spreadsheet_id}:batchUpdate`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spreadsheet_id` | string | yes | Spreadsheet id, the long string in its link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit. |
| `requests` | object[] | yes | Sheets API Request objects, e.g. [{"sortRange": {"range": {"sheetId": 0, "startRowIndex": 1}, "sortSpecs": [{"dimensionIndex": 2, "sortOrder": "DESCENDING"}]}}]. Indexes are 0-based, end indexes exclusive. |

## Run it yourself

AnythingMCP is open source (AGPL-3.0). [Run it with Docker](../../../README.md#run-it-yourself), open **Connectors → Store**, pick **Google Sheets** and enter `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, then add your MCP server URL to the AI client.
